**Michael Bayer ([@zzzeek](https://github.com/zzzeek)) wrote:**

5 years, 16 watchers, 10 votes, zero pull requests :(.    

Here is what "impl-specific hook" means:

1. go into autogen/render.py

2. go into def _repr_type.    right below where it checks for a _user_defined_render(), we do another check, just like that, against the "impl", which is the thing in alembic/ddl/impl.py -> DefaultImpl.   With Postgresql it's an alembic.ddl.postgresql.PostgresqlImpl.   In _repr_type, this object is right there at `autogen_context.migration_context.impl`.   if it returns False, keep going.  If it returns a string, use it.

3. DefaultImpl gets a new method _render_type(type_obj, autogen_context) that returns False.

4. PosgresqlImpl gets a new method _render_type(type_obj, autogen_context) that looks for ARRAY and then makes the string.  Make sure it consults autogen_context.opts['sqlalchemy_module_prefix'] too.

5. new test is added in test_autogen_render.py -> AutogenRenderTest.   Look at test_repr_dialect_type for a general dialect-specific type test.

6. *run* *the* *test* to make sure it works!

Adds a new codepath into render._repr_type() that will consult

the exisiting repr() is combined with a replace featuring
the full autogen render of the nested type.

issue.title: Autogenerate generates Integer() instead of sa.Integer() when used with a dialect

labels.name: duplicate
labels.description: This issue or pull request already exists

repository.name: alembic
repository.description: A database migrations tool for SQLAlchemy.

issue.body:
**Migrated issue, originally created by bekt ([@bekt](https://github.com/bekt))**

I haven't tested with other dialects or types, but:


```py
from sqlalchemy.dialects import postgresql

class Car(db.Model)
    __tablename__ = 'cars'
    id = db.Column(db.Integer, primary_key=True)
    parts = db.Column(postgresql.ARRAY(db.Integer))
```

generates:

```py
...
from alembic import op
import sqlalchemy as sa
from sqlalchemy.dialects import postgresql

def upgrade():
    ### commands auto generated by Alembic - please adjust! ###
    op.create_table('cars',
    sa.Column('id', sa.Integer(), nullable=False),
    sa.Column('parts', postgresql.ARRAY(Integer()), nullable=True),
    sa.PrimaryKeyConstraint('id')
    )
    ### end Alembic commands ###
...
```

Line `postgresql.ARRAY(Integer()` should be `postgresql.ARRAY(sa.Integer())`.


*db is a SQLAlchemy instance in the context of a Flask app.

Here's the relevant except from the model file and the resulting line in the migration

```
class MyModel(Base):
    id = Column(Integer, primary_key=True)
    email = Column(String, nullable=False, index=True, unique=True)
    codes = Column(postgresql.ARRAY(String), nullable=False)

 # Generates the following upgrade in a migration
def upgrade():
    op.create_table(my_model',
    sa.Column('id', sa.Integer(), nullable=False),
    sa.Column('email', sa.String(), nullable=False),
    # Note that it is postgresql.ARRAY(String(), ...)
    sa.Column('codes', postgresql.ARRAY(String()), nullable=False),
    sa.PrimaryKeyConstraint('id')
    )
   ...
```

As written this yields an error because the codes column should be declared as `postgresql.ARRAY(sa.String(), ...)`.  (Note the missing `sa.` above
